_note: Act 1 opening (docs/01_VISION_AND_WORLD.md section 6). Steps run in order; goal types: releaseSpecies (distinct species released at a spot), catchSpecies (each listed species landed at a spot; spot "" = anywhere; optional minCm, night), ledgerSpecies (count distinct species in the Ledger), pay (a button in Field notes), none (end of what exists so far).

steps.title: First survey
steps.intro: Morning. Odile Marsh, Cedar Shoals Fisheries Trust. You're the new hire, so you get the pond. I need five species out of it, measured and released. Not kept. Released. The Trust needs data, not dinner.
steps.done: Five species. Huh. Wren used to say a pond tells you everything if you ask it properly. Come by the boathouse, Teodor's been eyeing that old rowboat of hers. The Trust pays $30 for the survey.

page.title: Wren's page: The Station Pond, April
page.text: Bluegill bed in the shallows when the water climbs past 21 degrees. The big bass sit in the shade of the lily pads and wait for them to get careless. So do I. The pond is small but it is honest: whatever you learn here, the sea will test.

steps.title: The Teal
steps.intro: Wren's rowboat, the Teal. Hull's sound, oarlocks are shot, transom's soft. Sixty dollars in parts and I'll have her floating by tomorrow. Then you can row up to the spring run like she used to.

goal.button: Pay Teodor for the Teal's repairs ($60)

steps.done: There she is. Row easy, the spring run's clear as gin and the mullet will see you coming a mile off.

page.title: Wren's page: The Teal
page.text: Bought her for forty dollars and a cooler of mullet. She leaks a little on the left, which keeps me humble. A small boat goes where the fish are, not where the ramps are.

steps.title: Spring run survey
steps.intro: The spring run holds 22 degrees all year, so in a cold snap half the coast piles in there. Get me a mullet, a sheepshead and a redear out of Kings Bay. Measured. Then we'll talk about what Wren left in that bay.
steps.done: Good numbers. Better than good. I found something in the boathouse while you were out: another of Wren's pages, tucked in the Teal's seat locker. The Trust pays $50 for the survey.

page.title: Wren's page: Kings Bay, a January cold front
page.text: Snook stacked in the spring boils like cordwood, waiting out the cold. Manatees above them. Everything alive on this coast knows where the warm water is. The Lantern rose again over the caves last night, Mze says. It moves with the dark. Something old follows it up.

steps.title: The Saturday weigh-in
steps.intro: You're the Trust kid, right? Junie Alcott, bait and tackle. Every Saturday I weigh the biggest bass anybody brings in, and Dale Pruitt's 41 centimetre fish has sat on top of my board since March. He reminds me. Daily. Bring me a Florida bass of 42 or better, from anywhere, and you knock him off.
steps.done: Look at the shoulders on that. Dale's going to sulk for a month. Your name's on the board, and the prize is forty dollars. Spend it here.

page.title: Wren's page: Junie's board, 1998
page.text: Junie bet me a dozen shiners I couldn't beat her husband's bass. I did, on a plastic worm I'd chewed half off. She paid up and has never once let me forget I chewed it. Big bass want it slow. Slower than that.

steps.title: The old river
steps.intro: Wren's notes keep circling back to a bend on the Suwannee below Old Town. Gar, bowfin, warmouth: fish that were old when the dinosaurs were young. Four species out of that bend, measured and released. And mind the eels, they're endangered.
steps.done: Four from the old river. You're starting to fish like her, you know. There was a page folded into the logbook under 'Suwannee'. I think she meant you to find it. The Trust pays $60 for the survey.

page.title: Wren's page: The Suwannee, August
page.text: The river is the colour of strong tea and older than anything that swims in it. Gar hang under the surface like sticks until you look twice. Bowfin gulp air and fear nothing. A sturgeon jumped by the bluff at dusk, all two metres of it, and came down like a dropped piano. Released everything. The river keeps its own ledger.

steps.title: The night shift
steps.intro: Half of what lives in these waters only moves after dark, and the Trust has no night data at all. A channel catfish and an American eel, both caught after dark. Anywhere. A sinker on the bottom, a lantern, and patience. Release the eel, it's endangered.
steps.done: Night records. The board at the Trust will think I made them up. You can sleep now. Probably.

page.title: Wren's page: After dark
page.text: Catfish taste the water the way we see it: the whole river is a map of smells to them. An eel came up my line once and over my wrist like a cold rope. I sat on the bank until the frogs started again.

steps.title: The annual report
steps.intro: The Trust's annual report is due and our species list is embarrassing. Twelve species in your Ledger and I can show the board this coast is still worth paying for. Anything, anywhere: it's the variety that counts.
steps.done: Twelve. The board renewed us for another year, and asked who you were. I told them you were Wren's replacement. Nobody argued.

page.title: Wren's page: Why a Ledger
page.text: Every fish I catch goes in the book: where, when, how long, what it took. My father thought it was madness. But a river doesn't tell you it's dying. It just gets quieter, one name at a time, and only a ledger notices.

steps.title: The Lantern
steps.intro: Mze called from the boat ramp. He says the Lantern rose over the spring caves at Kings Bay again last night, and the snook came up to meet it, the way Wren wrote. I don't believe in it. Go anyway. A snook from Kings Bay, after dark. Bring heavy line.
steps.done: You saw it too, didn't you. Don't tell the board. There's one more of her pages. It was in the Teal's bilge the whole time, sealed in a bag.

page.title: Wren's page: The Lantern
page.text: Not a boat, not a star. It rises from the vents under Kings Bay on the darkest nights, and every big fish in the spring lifts toward it like a congregation. I have followed its light up this whole coast. It goes north in summer. I am going with it.

steps.title: Wren's road
steps.intro: Wren's next page points north, to a lodge on Lake of the Woods. We'll need a truck that runs and a reason the Trust can afford it. (More of the Ledger's road arrives in later updates.)
